relations.subject: index:index-replica
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - distributesLoadVia. Note this is a DIFFERENT mechanism from the round-robin over duplicate indexes on indexing-and-query-perf.md: there the artifacts are separate indexes with identical definitions, here they are copies of one index, and the page calls it load-balancing rather than round-robin. Same predicate, deliberately, so phase 2 can see the two mechanisms side by side.
relations.evidence: **High Performance**: If original and replica copies are available, incoming queries are load-balanced across them.

relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - hasExecutionConstraint. The availability claim: losing one Index Service node does not lose access to replicated indexes.
relations.evidence: **Availability**: If one Index Service node is lost, the others continues to provide access to replicated indexes.

relations.subject: index:index-replica
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - createsOnAction, for the self-healing behaviour: replacement replicas are assigned to Index Service nodes as they are added, until the required count is restored.
relations.evidence: If the number of nodes running the Index Service decreases, and index replicas are lost, Couchbase Server progressively assigns replacement index replicas to all Index Service nodes subsequently added to the cluster, until the required number of index replicas again exists for each replicated index.

relations.subject: n1ql:createindex-with-nodes-num_replica
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - offersConfigurationChoice, for the `nodes` attribute used alone: placement is explicit and replica count is implied by the node list.
relations.evidence: In the `WITH` clause, use the `nodes` attribute to specify the destination nodes. When you use this attribute by itself, the index is placed on one of the destination nodes, and one replica is placed on each of the others.

relations.subject: n1ql:createindex-with-nodes-num_replica

notable_absence.finding: This is the page that describes what happens to indexes when nodes are lost, restarted, failed over and rolled back, and it names NO state at all - neither the promoted `index-state` values (online, offline, building, pending, deferred...) nor the promoted `indexer-node-state` values (ready, pause, warmup, 'n mutations remaining') nor storage-modes.md's undefined Active/Warmup/Paused. It says an index is 'rebuilt from the snapshots retained on disk' and never says what state it is in while that happens, even though storage-modes.md answers exactly that question for memory-optimized indexes ('these indexes remain in the `Warmup` state'). So the two pages in this batch that describe restart-and-rebuild give two different amounts of information about it, and the one filed under 'Availability and Performance' gives less. Second absence: the load-balancing claim ('incoming queries are load-balanced across them') is never given a mechanism, a granularity, or a settings surface - contrast indexing-and-query-perf.md, which does name the mechanism for the duplicate-index case ('round-robin'). Third: index partitioning gets a four-bullet benefits list and no syntax, no default, no partition count, no constraint, and no cross-reference to the fact that partial indexes can be used to hand-roll the same thing (which indexing-and-query-perf.md suggests in four bullets of its own). Fourth: nothing states whether replicas and partitions interact, though both are on this page and both place index copies on nodes.

cross_component_finding: Five defects, three of them link-level. (1) WRONG ANCHOR ON A SETTINGS LINK: 'You can change the index replication settings using the [UI](../manage/manage-settings/general-settings.md#index-storage-mode)' - the anchor is `#index-storage-mode`, which is the STORAGE MODE section of General Settings, not the replication settings. A reader following the UI link for replica counts lands on the memory-optimized-vs-standard control. The CLI and REST links in the same sentence are correct. (2) TWO BROKEN ANTORA XREFS SURVIVE THE MARKDOWN CONVERSION: '[Index Service](#services-and-indexes/services/index-service.adoc)' in the first line of Index Replication renders as a fragment link to a nonexistent anchor. storage-modes.md has the identical defect shape ('#services-and-indexes/indexes/index-replication.adoc'), so this is a systematic conversion failure for cross-module xrefs in this module, not a one-off typo. (3) GRAMMAR ERROR IN A BOLD BENEFIT BULLET: 'If one Index Service node is lost, the others continues to provide access to replicated indexes.' - 'the others continues'. Quoted verbatim above. (4) THE SCAN-CONSISTENCY ENUM IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS THE MODULE: this page lists four values with full semantics; index-lifecycle.md lists three and omits `statement_plus`; index-lifecycle.md also calls the parameter 'index consistency' in one bullet and 'scan consistency' in the next, while this page uses 'Index Consistency' as its section heading and 'scan consistency' for the parameter. So the module has a section title, a parameter name, and a partial enum that do not line up, and index-lifecycle.md links to this page's anchor for the definition. (5) An `at_plus` reader is under-served on both pages: this page's definition ('requiring indexes first to be updated to the timestamp of the last update') does not explain where that timestamp comes from, and storage-modes.md then says queries with `consistency=at_plus` can FAIL if the specified timestamp exceeds the last one processed - a failure mode this page's definition does not admit exists.
cross_product_finding: The same page is extracted at cloud/indexes/index-replication.json (Capella) and server/7.2/learn/services-and-indexes/indexes/index-replication.json (Server 7.2, under `learn/`), and I reused four ids from those records (`index:index-consistency`, `index:index-snapshot`, `index:index-rollback`, `index:rollback-snapshot-revert`) plus `n1ql:createindex-with-nodes-num_replica`. Product-level divergence worth flagging: this Server page states the Enterprise Edition gating twice in bold admonitions, which a Capella page cannot meaningfully do (Capella has no editions), so any cross-product merge of `index:index-replication` will find `requiresEdition` present on the Server side and absent on the Capella side for reasons of product shape rather than feature difference. Second: this page's REST example posts `numReplica=2` to `/settings/indexes` on `localhost:8091`, a cluster-admin surface that does not exist for a Capella user - so the minted `index:num-replica-setting` is a Server-only concept even though the per-statement `num_replica` attribute is not. Phase 2 should not fold the setting into the WITH attribute for that reason as well as the precedence reason.
